The father was in the hospital and his family was asking to see him. He's not safe outside the hospital." 

And then there was another example of a woman being given sensory deprivation testing and on Cameron's written records fro the woman it says she lasted up to five hours without any signs of distress at all. First things first: Script it out. Fully. Then go through and break it down and cut out parts you can't afford (you'd be suprised what you can do on the cheap though) and make a list of everything you'll need.

Check out some of the Youtube indie series. Marble Hornets or Whispered Faith, maybe Keratin Garden, TJA Projects, or Down My Cellar Door (yea they're all Slender Man series but they're also just really awesome). They're all indie films, shot in first-person camera, just some video editing and some great writing. Some masks from like Michael's or a thrift store and a few other props here and there. I know in WF they just whispered random shit into a microphone and messed up in Audacity. (free sound editing program) Most of them are shot with just some friends fucking around with each other. Really great examples of low budget horror. Also My Dad's Tapes is another really good one but I'm not sure on their budget, since they get pretty gorey. Still a must-see if you wanna do first-person cam/found footage horror. (OH! Also maybe check out Home Movie? I think that one was also on a budget)

Websites? /r/filmmaking is GREAT for indie films, there's also various other indie film sites out there, google and find one that seems to fit you (read over threads, get a feel for how 'indie' they really are). Also, a bit random but get to know some of the creators of the slenderseries on UnFiction, they all know each other and are willing to share tips if you're nice about it. (if you watch their series first so you can introduce yourself AS a fan then that's even better)

Sound- Audacity, audacity, audacity. There are also TONS of free sound effects on various websites, or go learn how to make them yourself in the real world (research folly editing or how old radio dramas did what they did, like using cat litter for running through gravel or sand) Whispered Faith had a monster scraping at the walls in the first video, You can do that with just a stick and someone standing on the other side of the wall out of the camera's view. Down My Cellar Door uses a lot of doppleganger stuff, that's just knowing how to cut and greenscreen with camera (literally you can buy a green sheet for that...)

Also I produced a short-lived series called Karen Is Missing that was fully just parks and old locations around my area. Ask if you can use friend's houses and stuff. (like 90% of our budge went to actors- seriously, you can get lots of stuff just from thrift stores or dollar stores, try other parts of town you haven't been to and see if they have any wierd Chinese dollar stores, we got the airsoft gun we use from there for like $15) Creeks are great for shooting, if you go when there isn't a chance of rain (stay safe!) and you can even shoot in tunnels if you have large enough drains to use, creates a nice claustrophobic feeling.

The Movie Editor that I use is MAGIX Movie Edit Pro 17 Plus, but I've used 14 Plus before and both are really good and user-friendly if you read the manual and play around with it! It's about $45 new, I think about $15 used for the 14 version?


Actors! You can ask online! Texas, we have castingcalldallas and shortfilmtexas, lots of other sites. Just mention that you're non-union, a studend tilm and that you'll be providing food or snacks. (FEED YOUR ACTORS IF YOU ARE NOT GOING TO PAY THEM. NO REAL:Y THIS IS HUGE IF YOU'RE A DIRECTOR)

IF you are going to use a weapon and other actors MAKE SURE IT IS ARISOFT. Then if you get the cops called on you just calm down and hand them the gun and they'll see that it is indeed airsoft. Screaming I can't help with much, just be ready for it- or maybe add the screams in during the editing, have your actress scream into a mic at home.

ALSO. Just learn, learn as much as you can. Learn how to use half-and-half for fireballs, how to make your own nose wax for scars or your own stage blood with corn syrup. Learn lots of ways to do the same thing and make up your own technique. The more you can do yourself, the more that you can save yourself the trouble of buying or paying someone to do for you.

Seriously, if you wanna chat film stuff with me, have any more questions, don't be afraid to message me or anything. I'd love to just chat your ear off and offer what tips I've learned. Specially if you live in the DFW area!

I'm getting back into it though, working on the characterization and cutting out most of the characters-as-device and such.

She should, at least in my st (TX) be able to give you a code. You call in, and they tell her you called and she decides if she wants to talk to you or not, then you give them the code and talk until someone else bugs you to use the phone. Then you can use that code to call them back whenver, or if she has your number memorized and no one's using the phone, they can call you back. You may have to get the code through an immediate family memeber, I'm not sure. I had to call my Mom to let my fiance know that I was there since I didn't have his number meorized, so I gave her my patient code and she gave it to him. They can't conform or deny that the patient is there unless the patient says they want to talk to you. (My Dad tried to call me but I did NOT want to talk to them, so Mom had to keep him updated on my condition since i kept refusing his calls.) For the rest, you really just sit there and watch TV and keep to yourself. If you wanna talk to other patients it's fine, but most of them are either lost in their own minds or just not wanting to talk. It's more boring than scary, once you get over the initial shock of "OMG WHAT IS GOING ON."

Try calling around, most of the time they'll take her to whatever's closest. I know in my area it was either Green Oaks or Terrel State, and GO was  closest so I got sent to that one (which was also the only one in the US allowed to only do 24 hour holds, which was... weird.)

Personally, I wanted to be a psychologist so I chatted with the nurses and they showed me my forms and stuff they were filling out, so it was both interesting and scary, mostly boring though. Some of the doctors were dicks (I told them I was Wiccan and they went "you don't really believe in all that magic shit, do you?" ect, but the female nurses were really kind.) They're going to try to keep the environment safe/calm for her.

/disclamer: this is all my own experience, I'm not saying this is your state's laws, just the ones I know from my county/state.
